_comment: Dependencies allowed by exception under P17 / ADR-0004. `categoryB` = weak-copyleft (LGPL/MPL/EPL); `undeclared` = the package.json carries no `license` field at all (pnpm reports "Unknown"), so a human read the licence file the package ships and recorded it here. Each entry is a deliberate, isolated, reviewed allowance — NOT a place to silence Cat-X (GPL/AGPL/source-available). `package` is matched by exact name OR name-prefix (covers per-platform variants); a row with `"ecosystem": "pypi"` covers a Python package and is matched by exact name. gate:licenses fails on any Cat-B or undeclared dep not listed here, npm or Python. `operatorSupplied` = an optional runtime the operator downloads under its vendor's terms; under P17 it is not a dependency (ADR-0039). A row with `link` names the native library a tracked binding.gyp links; gate:vendor-payload fails on any linked library without a row, and on an `operatorSupplied` row whose contracts are not sealed.

categoryB.reason: libvips native binary behind `sharp`. LGPL is weak copyleft; it would be used unmodified and dynamically linked (a separate prebuilt .so/.dylib that sharp's binding loads at runtime), which ADR-0004 treats as Category B; FINOS lists LGPL as Category X. It reaches two npm locks outside the pnpm tree, as an optional dependency of next that only the image optimizer loads: clients/terminal, which turns the optimizer off (next.config.ts images.unoptimized), and the retiring 0.10 dashboard (services/dashboard, not built by this line), whose next/image uses it. The pnpm tree has none: @huggingface/transformers' sharp is overridden by @vexa/no-image-backend (pnpm-workspace.yaml).
categoryB.disposition: Logged exception for the terminal's build stage only. Not in any runtime image: clients/terminal/Dockerfile (deps-prod) and Lite's terminal-builder remove sharp and @img/*, and vexaai/vexa-bot and vexa-lite's bot tree load the stand-in. gate:image-licenses holds all three.

categoryB.reason: Native CSS transform/minification engine used by the Next/Tailwind toolchain. MPL applies to the unmodified dependency files, not to Vexa source or generated CSS.
categoryB.disposition: Logged exception; dependency remains an isolated build/runtime package managed by pnpm.
categoryB.scope: terminal build only (devDependency via @tailwindcss/postcss); absent from every runtime image

categoryB.reason: Qt 5 Core, linked by the optional native meeting wrapper (`pkg-config --libs Qt5Core` in core/meetings/services/bot/runtime/native-meeting/native/binding.gyp) because the operator-supplied meeting SDK requires it. Used unmodified and loaded as a shared library at runtime, never statically linked. Vexa ships neither Qt nor the compiled wrapper: the operator installs Qt from their distribution, or uses the copy the SDK bundles under qt_libs, and builds the wrapper outside every image.
categoryB.disposition: Logged exception; not redistributed in any Vexa artifact (gate:vendor-payload).

categoryB.reason: The Mozilla CA bundle packaged for Python. MPL-2.0 is file-level weak copyleft: it covers certifi's own files, which are used unmodified, and nothing of Vexa's. It reaches every Python service that makes outbound TLS calls through httpx, requests or botocore.
categoryB.disposition: Logged exception; installed unmodified from PyPI as a dependency, never vendored into this repository. Listed in NOTICE.
categoryB.scope: every Python image except flows: admin-api, agent-api, agent worker, credential-broker, gateway, mcp, meeting-api, runtime, transcription, and the matching vexa-lite venvs

categoryB.reason: Progress-bar library pulled in by faster-whisper (model download progress). Its MPL-2.0 files make the package Category B as a whole; they are used unmodified, and MPL's file-level copyleft does not reach Vexa code.
categoryB.disposition: Logged exception; installed unmodified from PyPI as a dependency, never vendored. Listed in NOTICE.
categoryB.scope: transcription service only (core/meetings/services/transcription, a direct dependency of faster-whisper)

undeclared.reason: Colour-manipulation library, a direct dependency of mermaid (diagram rendering in the terminal's doc/editor/chat renderers, Vexa-ai/vexa#1617). Its package.json omits the `license` field, so pnpm reports it as "Unknown"; the package itself ships `license` verbatim — "The MIT License (MIT), Copyright (c) 2019-present Fabio Spampinato, Andrew Maney" — and its repository (github:fabiospampinato/khroma) states MIT. Cat A on the text, undeclared only in the metadata.
undeclared.disposition: Logged exception; read from the shipped licence file at khroma@2.1.0. Re-read it if the package is ever upgraded across a major.
undeclared.scope: @vexa/terminal (transitive via mermaid, bundled into the client)

operatorSupplied.name: Zoom Meeting SDK for Linux
operatorSupplied.reason: Optional native meeting backend. The operator downloads the SDK from Zoom under Zoom's own terms, which restrict bot and notetaker use, and holds that licence. Vexa never commits, vendors, downloads or bakes it into any artifact; it is off by default and absent from every default entrypoint and from compose, Helm, Lite and stock dispatch; the bot reaches it only from a disposable child process over the sealed sdk-join.v1 and sdk-capture.v1 contracts. Under P17 it is not a dependency.
